title: Quantized Slab Ladders & Capacity Cushion Pilot for Dedicated GPU Packaging
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Experiment to validate a new dedicated GPU packaging construct: 'Quantized Slab Ladders' paired with a small configurable 'Capacity Cushion' that absorbs short spikes without forcing customers into higher reserved tiers. Objective is to find a price/performance curve that reduces churn on committed plans, improves revenue predictability, and reduces emergency overage support. This ticket covers pricing experiments, contract language variants for enterprise SQ, and the pilot rollout to three strategic customers.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 slab tiers (S/M/L) with quantized commit steps and documented unit economics
Design a Capacity Cushion that can be purchased as an add-on or auto-consumed with burst credits and clear billing telemetry
Legal-approved contract language for cushion consumption and preemption behavior included in SQ answers
Pilot with 3 customers for at least 6 weeks and measure: utilization smoothing, overage events reduced by >=30%, and NPS change for capacity-related incidents
Engineering changes merged: cushion allocator, minute-level autoscale hooks, and billing tag propagation; perf SLOs validated

pricing_model_summary: Base slab: S=4 GPU-hours/minute equivalent at $X/hr, M=10 GPU-hours/minute eq at $Y/hr, L=20 GPU-hours/minute eq at $Z/hr. Quantized steps reduce SKU proliferation (customers buy in discrete ladders). Capacity Cushion sold as fixed hourly buffer (e.g., 10% of slab size) or as burst credits charged at surcharge rate (1.7x token unit cost). Finance modeled scenarios: cushion reduces overage incidents by 30-60% depending on workload burstiness; price floor set to maintain >18% gross margin after infra and ops. Sensitivity: if average cushion utilization >40% sustained for 7 days, recommend auto-upgrade flow to next slab with pro-rated billing.
engineering_requirements: Allocator: implement cushion-aware scheduler that can absorb short spikes without moving customers to preemptible lanes
Autoscale hooks: support minute-level scale-up/down and grace windows tied to cushion consumption
Billing: tag requests with slab_id and cushion_consumed for token-level attribution and invoice line items
Observability: new dashboards for cushion utilization, per-customer cushion debt, and p99 latency under cushion usage
SLA: formalize p99/p95 targets per slab with documented fallback behaviors
sq_questions_highlight: How is cushion usage audited? Customer requests detailed logs for cushion consumption and billing events.
Data residency: confirm cushion-related metrics do not cross region boundaries for regulated customers.
KMS/keys: if cushion enables local caching, confirm keys remain customer-managed in Private deployments.
Preemption semantics: document exactly when and how cushion will be drained and customer notified; include replay/consistency guarantees.
Incident response: include cushion-specific runbooks (billing disputes, over-provisioning edge cases)
